turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. The queue was hectic, sorry you sat so long.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, since half past eight. I'm tired, let's just do this.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): What did they call you in for?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The sister at the day hospital phoned. I must come about the blood test, the INR. I'm not even sick.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): I've got it here. INR this morning is 4.2. For the atrial fibrillation we want between 2 and 3, so that's high.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): 4.2. Yoh. All this for a number. And it's warfrin, five milligrams, every night after supper, for the AF, years now, if that's your next question.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): It was, yes. Five milligrams at night for the fibrillation. Have you actually taken it every night, no misses?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. Most nights, but I'm not swearing to every one.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): So it says every night on the script, but you're not sure you've managed every dose. What else are you on?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine, five milligrams, for the pressure, in the morning. The cholesterol one at night, uh, simvastaten, twenty. Sugar tablets, metforman, five hundred, twice a day with food. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning.

[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll read that back. Amlodipine five milligrams each morning for the pressure, simvastatin twenty milligrams at night, metformin five hundred milligrams twice a day with food, warfarin five at night, and the Ayurvedic powder in the morning. Did I get that?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, that's it. Don't lecture me on the powder. My wife gets it from the shop in town, she swears by it.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): No lecture. Did the GP start you on an antibiotic recently?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, four days ago, at the clinic. Amoxicillin, five hundred milligrams, three times a day, for this cough. Seven day course, so I've got three days left.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Amoxicillin can push the INR up when you're on warfarin. How's the cough itself?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Still there. Dry, worse at night when I lie down. Been four days.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with it?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding? Bruises, nose, gums, blood in the urine, black stools?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. I'm not bleeding.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): And greens. Spinach, morogo, that sort of thing. Same as usual?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. My daughter said greens are poison with warfarin, so I stopped the morogo and the spinach. Two weeks of nothing, and I used to eat it most days. I miss it, hey.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shame, that advice has worked against you. Cutting the greens out lifts the INR as well. A similar portion most days is safer than none.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Whatever. Nobody told me that.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness, or the heart racing?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not a clear yes, I won't chase it. Right. Blood pressure is 138 over 82, pulse is 76 and irregular, which fits the fibrillation, and the saturation is 97 percent.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 138 bad? And listen, I said I wasn't bleeding, that was wrong. My gums bleed every time I brush, the last three or four days. There's a bruise on my right thigh that came up from nothing.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): 138 over 82 is acceptable, and the irregular pulse is the old fibrillation, not new. Gum bleeding when you brush, and that thigh bruise, do fit a high INR. Can I look?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Outer thigh. Don't poke.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can see a bruise on the outer right thigh. The gums aren't bleeding while you're sitting here.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, it's when I brush. Ag.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Noted. Any blood in the urine, or black stools?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Urine's normal. Stools are a normal colour, not black.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None. The amoxicillin hasn't given me a rash or anything.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression, nothing firmer, is that the INR of 4.2 is up because of the amoxicillin and because you stopped the greens. The gum bleeding and the thigh bruise sit with that. I can't prove more today.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): So what must I actually do? I've got to fetch my grandson, and the robot by the school is a nightmare now.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): From tonight, stop the five milligrams. Take warfarin four milligrams once a day after supper, still for the fibrillation. Finish the three days of amoxicillin left, and don't take an extra warfarin if you missed one.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Four milligrams, fine. I'm not stopping the powder though. My wife will have a fit.

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then keep the powder exactly as it is, and don't increase it. I'd rather you paused it, I don't know what's in it, but I won't fight you today. And put a usual portion of morogo or spinach back most days, the same sort of amount, not a binge.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Steady greens, same powder. Ja. I heard you.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll book a repeat INR in a week, and a follow-up with me the same day. Reception will give you the lab form.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): A week. If the gums pour with blood before that, I'm not sitting in this queue for fun.

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the gums bleed heavily, or you get a bad nosebleed, go straight to casualties and don't wait. The visit in a week still stands. To say it back, four milligrams from tonight, finish the antibiotic, greens steady, powder unchanged, blood test and review in a week.

spec.situation: Older patient on warfarin for atrial fibrillation; INR result read aloud; antibiotic started elsewhere; green leafy diet changes; dose adjusted and recheck in a week.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Dose/frequency/indication stated, but adherence is uncertain; not clearly currently taken every night.
bad.text: warfarin (dose=5 mg, frequency=every night after supper, indication=atrial fibrillation, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Completed INR for warfarin monitoring is supported, but transcript doesn't say doctor requested it.
